name: Paystack
tagline: Stripe-owned African payment platform serving 200,000+ businesses in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa and Cote d'Ivoire.
shortDescription: Lagos-based payment platform, a Stripe company since 2020, covering cards, bank transfer, USSD, mobile money and Apple Pay across five African markets. Nigerian local transactions cost 1.5% + NGN 100, hard-capped at NGN 2,000, with no setup or monthly fees.
longDescription:
Paystack was founded in Lagos in 2015 by Shola Akinlade and Ezra Olubi, became the first Nigerian company through Y Combinator, and was acquired by Stripe in October 2020 for a reported 200 million dollars, the largest startup acquisition out of Nigeria at the time. Today it serves more than 200,000 businesses with merchant onboarding live in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa and Cote d'Ivoire, with Egypt and Rwanda in early access. It routes each market's real payment mix: cards, bank transfer, USSD, Visa QR and virtual accounts in Nigeria, M-PESA in Kenya, MTN and Orange mobile money in Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire, Capitec Pay and EFT in South Africa, plus Apple Pay.

Pricing and how it works

Pricing is pure pay-per-transaction with zero integration and zero maintenance fees. Nigerian local transactions cost 1.5% + NGN 100, with the NGN 100 waived under NGN 2,500 and total fees hard-capped at NGN 2,000, so a 10 million naira payment still costs at most NGN 2,000. International cards in Nigeria cost 3.9% + NGN 100. Ghana charges a flat 1.95%, Kenya 1.5% on M-PESA and 2.9% on local cards, and South Africa 2.9% + 1 rand plus VAT. Settlement is automatic and free: next working day in Nigeria and Ghana, two working days in Kenya and South Africa. Paystack charges no penalty for accepting a chargeback, though escalating a dispute to card-network arbitration carries the networks' own fees. In Nigeria it also sells card terminals, virtual accounts and identity verification APIs.

Who it is for

Paystack is the default choice for businesses in its five live markets that want reliable local acceptance with developer-grade APIs and 60+ platform integrations including Shopify, WooCommerce, Wix and BigCommerce. It cannot onboard merchants outside Africa, features vary noticeably between markets, and payout-delay complaints during compliance reviews are the main recurring criticism.

data.html:
For businesses operating in Africa, choosing a payment processor often comes down to more than card acceptance. Local payment methods, currencies, payouts, business onboarding, and the countries supported by the provider can all affect whether a platform works in practice.

Paystack is built around payments for businesses in African markets and is particularly relevant to startups, online businesses, and merchants selling locally or across supported markets.

Paystack Pricing by Country

Paystack pricing is not necessarily identical across every market.

When comparing costs, check the pricing applicable to your specific country and payment method.

Important costs can include:

  • Card transaction fees
  • Bank payment fees
  • International payment fees
  • Currency conversion
  • Payout-related costs

Paystack Supported Countries and Currencies

Country availability should be one of the first things an international business checks.

A processor can have excellent features but still be unsuitable if your business location, customers, or preferred settlement currency isn't supported.

Who Is Paystack Best For?

Paystack is particularly relevant to:

  • African startups
  • eCommerce businesses
  • SaaS companies
  • Online service businesses
  • Businesses collecting digital payments

Is Paystack Owned by Stripe?

Stripe acquired Paystack, but Paystack continues to operate as a payment technology platform focused on African markets.

Paystack Payout Times

Payout timing depends on the market, payment method, account setup, and applicable settlement rules. Businesses should confirm the current settlement schedule for their specific country.

faqs.question: How much does Paystack cost?
faqs.answer: There are no setup or monthly fees in any market. Nigerian local transactions cost 1.5% + NGN 100, with the NGN 100 waived under NGN 2,500 and fees hard-capped at NGN 2,000 per transaction; international cards cost 3.9% + NGN 100. Ghana charges a flat 1.95%, Kenya charges 1.5% on M-PESA and 2.9% on local cards, and South Africa charges 2.9% + 1 rand plus 15% VAT on fees.

faqs.question: Which countries can use Paystack?
faqs.answer: Merchant signup is live for businesses registered in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa and Cote d'Ivoire, with Egypt and Rwanda in early access. Businesses based in the US, UK, Europe or Asia cannot open a Paystack account, though merchants in the live markets can accept international cards from customers worldwide.

faqs.question: How fast does Paystack pay out?
faqs.answer: Settlement is automatic and free: next working day in Nigeria and Ghana, and two working days in Kenya and South Africa. Nigerian merchants can optionally settle international transactions in US dollars through a domiciliary account pilot, and Kenyan merchants can charge and settle international cards in either KES or USD.

faqs.question: Who owns Paystack?
faqs.answer: Stripe acquired Paystack in October 2020 for a reported 200 million dollars and it continues to operate as a Stripe company under its own brand. It marked ten years in January 2026 and remains headquartered in Lagos with offices across Africa, the US and Dubai.
